Problem
Nobody has checked real microphone capture, audio upload, the desktop-width layout, or speech recognition with real recordings in English, Chinese, German and Hindi. The redesigned frontend (#6) and the Gemini Live client (#22) are not built yet, so there is nothing to click through today.

Approach: tests first
Write the browser suite now, against a written frontend contract (data-testid hooks + data-state on the cat), so #6 / #22 are built to pass it. The tests are red until the UI lands, then they turn this manual checklist into a repeatable command.

Mic capture (Chromium fake audio device fed a real WAV): the recording that reaches /voice/transcriptions is a non-silent mono 16-bit WAV of the recorded length that the server accepts; mic tracks are released after stop; permission denied and no-mic show a recovery message and keep the typed flow usable.

Real recordings (opt-in, real Gemini key, recordings kept off git): WER/CER per language for en, zh, de, hi, once through the API and once through the browser mic.

# Browser and real-speech tests (issue #25)

Automated versions of the manual checks in [docs/VALIDATION.md](../../docs/VALIDATION.md): microphone capture,
audio upload, desktop layout, the Gemini Live voice client, and recognition of English, Chinese, German and Hindi
speech. They drive the shipped pages: the React app at `/app` (built from `web/`) and the original page at `/`.

## Run

```bash
pip install -r requirements-e2e.txt && python -m playwright install chromium
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e                      # 62 browser tests, no keys, about 75 s
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e -k live_voice --headed   # watch one file
```

The suite (re)builds `web/dist` whenever it is missing or older than a `web/` source (needs Node), so it always
tests your current frontend. `bash scripts/check.sh` skips the browser tests and runs only the speech-metric tests.
Layout screenshots land in `test-results/layout/` (git-ignored) for a human look.

## What runs, and how without hardware or keys

| File | Page | What it proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_browser_live_voice.py` | `/app/?live=1` | Consent before any token; ephemeral token on the constrained socket; mic off until the owner turns it on; audible 16 kHz PCM at real-time pace; mute sends `audioStreamEnd` and stops audio; transcripts as text (no HTML); model audio plays and an interruption flushes it; typed text goes over the socket; tool calls forwarded once, answered and rendered; `open_clinic_call` only offers the dialer; token failure, denied mic and dropped socket are explained; hang-up and drops release the mic |
| `test_browser_recording.py` | `/app/?live=1&voice=rest`, own voice | REST fallback: one audible mono 16 kHz WAV per spoken turn, accepted by the server's validator, in the chosen language; own-voice recorder plays back locally, uploads nothing, rejects under 10 s; denied mic explained |
| `test_browser_upload.py` | `/` | Audio upload (the React app has none): 48 kHz stereo, 44.1 kHz and 8 kHz WAVs play locally and are sent as mono 16-bit; too short, too long and non-audio files are explained and never sent; a new upload replaces the old; a recorded message is audible |
| `test_browser_layout.py` | `/app`, call screen, `/` | At 1280, 1440, 1920 and 390 px: no sideways scroll, no overlapping controls, WCAG 2.2 target size (with its spacing and inline-link exceptions), call controls on screen, app column centred on desktop, demo badge visible |

- **Microphone:** Chromium's fake capture device loops 2.5 s of speech-like sound and 2.5 s of silence, so a
  silent or broken capture path fails and voice-activity detection sees turns end.
- **Gemini Live:** the Live WebSocket is answered by `FakeLive` (`e2e_helpers.py`) in the real `@google/genai`
  wire format; `/live/tokens` and `/live/tool-calls` are mocked. The app's bundled SDK, AudioWorklet and playback
  run for real.
- **Server:** the real app runs with all provider keys blanked; tests mock only the provider-backed routes they need.
- Every browser test also fails on an unexpected console error.

## Real speech (opt-in, spends Gemini quota)

```bash
set -a; . ./.env; set +a     # GEMINI_API_KEY
export PAWSE_LIVE_SPEECH=1 PAWSE_RECORDINGS_DIR=/mnt/pawse-recordings
python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_real_recordings_api.py         # /voice/transcriptions (REST fallback path)
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_browser_real_speech.py   # spoken into the live call, real Gemini Live
```

`PAWSE_RECORDINGS_DIR/manifest.json` lists the recordings; they never go in git:

```json
{ "recordings": [
  { "file": "de-01.wav", "language": "de", "reference": "Meine Katze Mimi hinkt seit dem Sprung vom Schrank.",
    "speaker": "s1", "device": "laptop mic" }
] }
```

- At least 3 per language (`en`, `zh`, `de`, `hi`), ideally different speakers and devices. Recordings are personal
  data: collect them with the speaker's consent, keep them on `/mnt`, delete them when done.
- Mono 16-bit PCM WAV, 0.5 to 60 s, up to 3 MB: `ffmpeg -i in.m4a -ac 1 -ar 16000 -sample_fmt s16 de-01.wav`.
- `reference` is exactly what was said; write numbers the way they are spoken.

Pass bar ([speech_metrics.py](speech_metrics.py)): word error rate at most 0.15 (en), 0.20 (de), 0.30 (hi);
character error rate at most 0.20 (zh). Chinese must come back in Han characters and Hindi in Devanagari. Silence must
give an empty transcript. Per-recording results go to `test-results/speech-api.json`.

Synthetic speech is a pipeline smoke test, not an accuracy benchmark: `espeak-ng` English, German and Hindi work over
REST, but its Mandarin voice reads tone codes ("T1 F5 …") and Gemini Live barely recognises any of it. Use human
recordings to judge recognition.

--- name: document-download description: >- Robustly downloads web documents — direct PDFs, print-to-PDF renders of HTML-only pages, full-page screenshots, and embedded images extracted from pages/docs — into a manifest with full provenance (source URL, method, sha256, robots/deny-list check, poppler text-verification) and honest gaps for anything blocked/404/disallowed. Run when asked to download insurer AVB/ARB policy-terms PDFs for the competitive AVB library, archive citation-source documents (court decisions, statutes, AVB/ARB PDFs) for deep-legal-research, or pull "frontend pictures" (embedded UI screenshots inside competitor brochures/whitepapers/ feature PDFs) for competitive-design-pipeline. Fetch-only — never verifies citations, never fakes a blocked/404 as success. Not for live-site UI screenshot galleries (competitive-screenshots). triggers: phrases: - "download the AVB PDF" - "fetch the ARB terms" - "archive this court decision PDF" - "grab the policy terms document" - "extract screenshots from this brochure/whitepaper/PDF" - "document-download" negative: - "screenshot the competitor's product UI" - "capture live product screenshots" --- # document-download (`business-ops`) A **general, reusable document-fetch primitive**: given a list of target URLs, robustly download each as a real file — a PDF, a print-to-PDF render, a full-page screenshot, or extracted embedded images — with a manifest that records exactly what happened (method, hash, robots check, poppler text-verification) and never lies about a failure. **Three consumers, one fetch+manifest core, three target lists:** 1. **Competitive AVB library** — Rechtsschutz insurers' AVB/ARB policy-terms PDFs. 2. **Legal/academic research** — archive court-decision + ARB/AVB citation-source docs for [`deep-legal-research`](../deep-legal-research/SKILL.md) (fetch-only; this skill **never** verifies citations — that is deep-legal-research's `/api/attest` job, not this one's). 3. **Competitive design research** — competitor frontends described *inside* documents (brochures/whitepapers/feature PDFs with embedded UI screenshots); extract those "frontend pictures" for [`competitive-design-pipeline`](../competitive-design-pipeline/SKILL.md). **Gallery-only sibling:** live-site product-UI screenshot capture (no document/PDF angle) is [`competitive-screenshots`](../competitive-screenshots/SKILL.md) — use that instead when the target is a live page's UI, not a document. ## Bootstrap (root disk is small — everything heavy on `/mnt`) ```bash mkdir -p /mnt/document-download && cd /mnt/document-download export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/mnt/ms-playwright npm i playwright csv-parse # Chromium is likely already installed at that path (check before reinstalling): ls /mnt/ms-playwright 2>/dev/null || npx playwright install chromium cp /scripts/*.mjs scripts/ # copy this skill's scripts/ into the working dir ``` Downloads and manifests land under `/mnt/document-download//` — never committed. ## `targets.csv` input format ``` entity,category,doc_type,url,source_type,note Zurich,avb-library,AVB-Bauherren-Rechtsschutz,https://www.zurich.ch/.../avb-....pdf,direct-pdf, ``` - `entity` — the insurer/court/competitor name (used for the output subfolder). - `category` — free-text grouping (`avb-library`, `legal-research`, `design-research`, ...). - `doc_type` — what kind of document this is (used in the output filename). - `url` — the target. Quote any field containing a comma. - `source_type` — a hint for humans/logs (`direct-pdf`, `landing-page`, `html-terms`, `deny-listed`); the script auto-detects the real strategy regardless. - `note` — optional passthrough, becomes `citation_hint` in the manifest (never a `verified` claim — see deny-list section below). ## Workflow 1. **Author `targets.csv`** for your consumer (see worked examples below). Research URLs with WebSearch/WebFetch first — never guess a doc slug. 2. **Run the ladder:** `node scripts/run.mjs targets.csv `. Per row, incrementally writes `/manifest.json` + `/index.csv` (safe to Ctrl-C and resume — it skips any (entity, doc_type, url, method) already `ok` on disk with a matching size). 3. **Verify:** `node scripts/verify.mjs ` — batch report: magic-byte + poppler check per downloaded file, one summary table, no re-fetching. 4. **Report honestly** — how many rows `ok`, how many `gap` and why (blocked/404/robots/deny-list). Never recreate or fake a blocked/404 row as a success. ## Strategy ladder 1. **Direct PDF URL** → `ctx.request.get` → verify `%PDF-` magic bytes + size guard → write bytes to disk. (`method: direct-pdf`) 2. **Landing page** → render with Playwright → dismiss cookie/consent banners → DOM-scrape `` / download-flagged links → follow the first PDF-shaped link to strategy 1. (`method: scraped-link`) 3. **Browser-initiated download** — some target URLs have no `.pdf` extension (a docstore endpoint like `?accesscode=...` or `/media/72/download`) but the server serves the file as a browser attachment; `page.goto()` doesn't render a page at all — Chromium aborts the navigation and rejects with `"Download is starting"` while a `download` event fires. The ladder arms `page.on('download')`/`waitForEvent('download')` **before** every navigation that could hit this (strategy 1's fallback and strategy 2's landing-page render), catches that specific exception, awaits the pending download, and saves it via `download.saveAs()` — verified with the same `%PDF-` magic-byte check as strategy 1, then poppler-checked like any other PDF. Never crashes the row or mislabels a real document as a gap. (`method: browser-download`) 4. **HTML-only terms** (no PDF found/resolved, no download triggered) → `page.pdf()` print-to-PDF **and** a full-page screenshot. (`method: print-to-pdf` / `screenshot`) 5. **Embedded images** — always also attempted on the HTML-only path: pull large (`>=400x260`) non-data-URI `` assets out of the rendered page. (`method: image-extract`) 6. **robots.txt gate, per host, BEFORE scripting any fetch** — checked against Anthropic's published crawler names (`ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `Claude-User`); disallowed → record an honest gap row, do **not** fetch. Politeness: ~1-2 req/s (`DOC_DL_DELAY_MS` env, default 700ms between rows). Every strategy step runs the **deny-list check first** (see below), then the robots check, *before* any network call. ## Legal deny-list + ladder deference (CRITICAL) `lib.mjs` hard-codes a `DENYLIST_HOSTS` constant — **HARD-REFUSE** these hosts (robots-disallowed / CAPTCHA-gated policy) with a clear message, never silently retry with a different UA: `bger.ch`, `search.bger.ch`, `relevancy.bger.ch`, `openjur.de`, `gerichtsentscheidungen.li`, `gesetze.li`. `denylistCheck(url)` runs on **every** URL (including a link resolved by strategy 2) before any request. For legal sources generally, **defer to [`../deep-legal-research/sources.md`](../deep-legal-research/sources.md)** as the upstream source of truth for which hosts are allowed (opencaselaw, entscheidsuche, fedlex.admin.ch, eur-lex.europa.eu, de.openlegaldata.io, data.bka.gv.at/ris, hudoc.echr.coe.int, ...) — this skill does not duplicate that catalog. **This skill is fetch-only.** Its manifest **never** contains a `verified` or `confidence` field — those belong exclusively to deep-legal-research's verify subagent. A `citation_hint` passthrough field is allowed (unverified, just a note carried from `targets.csv`). ## Manifest schema Every downloaded artifact (or attempted-and-failed one) is one row in `/manifest.json` (+ flattened into `/index.csv`): | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | `entity, category, doc_type` | from `targets.csv` | | `source_url` | the actual URL fetched (may differ from the input `url` for `scraped-link`/`image-extract`) | | `requested_via` | `source_type` from the input row, or a note like `"scraped from "` | | `method` | `direct-pdf \| scraped-link \| browser-download \| print-to-pdf \| screenshot \| image-extract` | | `local_path, sha256, bytes` | null for a gap | | `http_status, content_type` | as observed | | `robots_check` | `{checked, allowed[, present]}` | | `pdf_text_ok` | poppler parsed non-trivial text (PDFs only; null for images) | | `citation_hint` | optional passthrough from `note`, **unverified** | | `fetched_at` | ISO timestamp | | `status` | `ok \| gap` | | `notes` | human-readable detail; for a gap, always states the reason | A **gap** = a row with empty `local_path` + a stated reason (blocked/404/robots/deny-list). **Never fake a blocked/404 as success.** ## Worked examples (one per consumer) **1. Competitive AVB library** — `entity=Zurich, category=avb-library, doc_type=AVB-Bauherren-Rechtsschutz, url=, source_type=direct-pdf` → strategy 1, `method: direct-pdf`, verified with poppler. **2. Legal/academic research (deep-legal-research)** — a citation-source URL for a BGE/BGH decision or an ARB PDF cited in a coverage annotation: `entity=BGH, category=legal-research, doc_type=IV-ZR-decision, url=, source_type=landing-page`. If the URL is `bger.ch`, it is refused (deny-list) — look up the same decision via `opencaselaw`/ `entscheidsuche` per `deep-legal-research/sources.md` instead, and feed *that* URL in. **3. Competitive design research** — a competitor's feature-brochure PDF or product page with embedded UI screenshots: `entity=Justis, category=design-research, doc_type=product-page, url=https://www.justis.ch/, source_type=html-terms` → no PDF found → print-to-pdf + screenshot + `image-extract` pulls out the large embedded UI images for `competitive-design-pipeline`'s capture stage. ## Details See [`reference.md`](reference.md) for: the deny-list/source-status convention in full, the poppler + print-to-PDF recipes, and a "best practices" note on direct-fetch vs headless print-to-PDF, robots.txt/ToS honesty for Anthropic's crawlers, and detecting login-wall/scanned PDFs. See [`evaluation.md`](evaluation.md) for activation scenarios across all three consumers. ## Keep this skill current - Strategy logic lives in `scripts/lib.mjs` (primitives) and `scripts/run.mjs` (orchestrator) — read them before changing ladder behavior; update this file if CLI flags, the manifest schema, or the working-dir contract change. - If `DENYLIST_HOSTS` changes (a new hard-refuse host, or deep-legal-research's allowed-host catalog moves), update both `lib.mjs` and the § Legal deny-list section above. - New failure class (a vendor blocking a new way) → add the winning fallback to [`reference.md`](reference.md) and a scenario to [`evaluation.md`](evaluation.md). - Catalog rows: [`README.md`](../README.md) and [`agent-skills-catalog.mdc`](../../rules/agent-skills-catalog.mdc). Legal posture: public, logged-out, non-personal, rate-limited (~1-2 req/s), robots.txt honored for Anthropic's crawler names, hard deny-list for known CAPTCHA/robots-disallowed hosts. evaluation.md reference.md scripts SKILL.md

content.text:
Two agents are now working in the background. Neither has finished, so there are no results yet.

**1. Fixing the 5 failing browser tests.** For each failure, the agent first decides whether the test or the UI is wrong, then fixes it test-first. That includes checking #61–#63 to see whether the own-voice recorder was removed on purpose; if it was, the agent stops and reports back rather than deleting those checks. It will also update `docs/VALIDATION.md`, add a nightly run of the browser suite that files an `e2e-red` issue when it fails (not a PR gate), then open a PR and squash-merge it if everything is green.

**2. Backup recordings from a public dataset.** The source is Google FLEURS: real people reading sentences aloud, with exact transcripts, under a CC-BY-4.0 license, in en, zh (Mandarin), de and hi. The agent takes 5 clips per language from different speakers, converts them to the WAV format the test expects, and stores them off git at `/mnt/pawse-recordings/fleurs/`. Each file gets a manifest entry with its source URL, license and sha256, plus a `PROVENANCE.md`. Then it runs the opt-in real-speech test once through the API, which is about 20 Gemini calls.
  - ⚠️ This is a backup, not a replacement. FLEURS sentences are read Wikipedia text, not "my cat is limping" in a worried voice on a phone mic. It gives a fair accuracy baseline per language, but the test sentences close to the demo still need your own recordings.

**business-ops `document-download` skill:** I read it. It's built for downloading PDFs and web pages, and its download steps rely on PDF-only checks, so it doesn't fit audio datasets. I'm reusing its provenance rules (the manifest fields, honest gaps) rather than copying the skill.

🛑 **Needs you:** auto mode blocked my GitHub issue edits as writes to an external system, even after your "ok". These were:
- a comment on #6 and on #22 linking `tests/e2e/README.md`
- changing `tests/browser` to `tests/e2e` in #25

Either add a permission rule for `gh issue comment` and `gh issue edit`, or run them yourself with `!`. I have the exact commands ready. The PR from agent 1 may hit the same block when it pushes; if so, I'll tell you.
